data.title: Pakistan Military Spokesperson: No Barrier to Iran Joining Mecca Defense Alliance; Decision Rests With Three Main Participants

data.title: Tankers Keep Crude Flowing Through Strait of Hormuz Despite Escalating Iranian Attacks
data.description: According to CNBC, crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz averaged nearly 11.1 million barrels per day in October, about 2% below September, despite an escalation in attacks on commercial ships. At least 30 vessels, mostly oil tankers, were hit as of Oct. 27, leaving at least 16 seafarers injured, according to the International Maritime Organization. Crude prices rose more than 13% this month, with Brent trading above $117 a barrel on Friday. Shippers have adapted by using a shuttle system that transfers oil from tankers exiting the strait to vessels in the Gulf of Oman. The system has helped flows rise more than 70% since July, but has increased costs: daily rates to hire a supertanker for the Gulf of Oman-to-Asia route climbed from $249,000 in early September to $931,000 by the first week of October. Tankers’ security depends on U.S. military air support, and the duration of that support remains uncertain.

data.description: According to Jin10, Dallas Fed President Lorie K. Logan said inflation not falling toward the Federal Reserve’s 2% target is “unacceptable.”

data.title: Dallas Fed President Lorie K. Logan: Clear Rate Target Would Help Markets Adapt to a Pause
data.description: According to Jin10, Dallas Fed President Lorie K. Logan said that if the final interest rate target is made clear in advance, markets and the economy can prepare and better adapt to a decision to temporarily pause rate hikes.

data.title: AI | David Baszucki Says Roblox AI Content Surged as Daily Users Fell 9%
data.description: Roblox CEO David Baszucki said AI-fueled content on the platform surged over the last three months, according to Bloomberg. Daily active users fell 9% last quarter and bookings declined 12% as the company rolled out tougher child-safety measures.

data.title: AI | Peter Singlehurst Says Anthropic’s Technical Edge Appeals to Long-Term Investors
data.description: Anthropic’s technical expertise, innovation and efficient use of compute set it apart in the AI landscape, said Peter Singlehurst, head of Baillie Gifford’s Private Companies Team, according to Bloomberg. Singlehurst said Anthropic’s governance structure, which gives its seven founders voting control, is good for long-term investors. He discussed the company with Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech.”

data.title: Godongwana Says Revised South African GDP Creates Fiscal Room
data.description: South African Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said an upward revision to gross domestic product, following a regular recalculation of how the economy is measured, creates fiscal headroom for the country, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Dallas Fed President Lorie K. Logan: Fed Needs at Least Two More 25-Basis-Point Hikes
data.description: According to Jin10, Dallas Fed President Lorie K. Logan said the Fed needs at least two more rate hikes of 25 basis points each.

data.title: STOCKS | Oil Majors Post $56.3 Billion Windfall as Fuel Prices Surge
data.description: Exxon Mobil, Chevron, BP, Shell and TotalEnergies exceeded third-quarter expectations, reporting combined adjusted net income of $56.3 billion as conflicts in the Persian Gulf and Russia drove refining results to record highs, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Gencom, White Bridge Capital Pay About $300 Million for Miami InterContinental
data.description: Gencom and White Bridge Capital bought the InterContinental hotel in downtown Miami for about $300 million, according to Bloomberg. The purchase marks the companies’ third joint hospitality deal in the past year.

data.title: STOCKS | Aspen Neuroscience Drops 2% After $140.6 Million US IPO
data.description: Aspen Neuroscience Inc., a Gilead-backed clinical-stage cell therapy developer, fell 2% after raising about $140.6 million in a US initial public offering, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Deutsche Bank's AI Dollar Warning Could Hit Bitcoin, Gold and Stocks
data.description: Deutsche Bank warned that an AI-led selloff could weaken the U.S. dollar alongside stocks, challenging the dollar’s usual safe-haven role when equities fall. Foreign investors own more than $20 trillion in U.S. shares, with about 90% of that value attributed to price appreciation, according to BeInCrypto. Deutsche Bank’s George Saravelos said falling U.S. real yields alongside weaker stocks and the dollar would signal markets cutting AI spending forecasts; Friday’s trading did not show that mix, as the dollar edged higher. Bitcoin and gold, both priced in dollars, could also be affected.

data.title: Tether Reports $191.5 Billion in Q3 Reserves and $1.5 Billion in Operating Profit
data.description:
Tether International, S.A. de C.V. released an assurance report prepared by BDO covering the third quarter of 2026, with data as of September 30. According to Odaily, Tether’s reserves totaled $191.5 billion at quarter-end, including $132.4 billion in direct and indirect U.S. Treasury holdings.

USD₮ issuance remained around $184 billion through the first three quarters, while cumulative net operating profit reached $4.5 billion. Third-quarter net operating profit was $1.5 billion, unchanged from the second quarter; U.S. Treasury securities and reverse repurchase agreements generated most of the revenue.

As of September 30, Tether reported total assets of $191.451 billion and total liabilities of $183.496 billion, leaving assets $7.955 billion above liabilities. Excess reserves increased to about $7.95 billion from $4.1 billion at the end of the second quarter.

data.title: St. Louis Fed President Alberto G. Musalem: Earlier Rate Hikes Could Reduce Economic Shock Risk
data.description: St. Louis Fed President Alberto G. Musalem said monetary policy and overall financial conditions remain accommodative, while inflation is still too high. According to Odaily, Musalem said inflation is unlikely to ease without Fed action and that raising rates earlier could reduce the risk of a shock to the broader economy.

data.title: AFT Sues Trump Administration Over Student Loan Forgiveness Delays
data.description: According to CNBC, the American Federation of Teachers sued the Trump administration Friday, alleging officials unlawfully blocked student loan forgiveness for tens of thousands of eligible borrowers. The lawsuit alleges Education Secretary Linda McMahon mismanaged the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program by miscounting payment timelines and failing to credit qualifying service. It also challenges delays in the PSLF Buyback program; 88,000 borrowers were still awaiting decisions as of the spring, according to a court filing. The Education Department said it was correcting coding errors from the Biden administration that had led to inaccurate payment counts.
